title: Abu Bakr's words
hook: Abu Bakr says whoever worshiped Muhammad, he has died, and whoever worships Allah, He lives (3:144)
carry: allah is alive and does not die

segments.voice: Yesterday, the highest companion: his last words in Aisha's small room, choosing the company of God. We sat in silence with it. Day two hundred ninety-one.

When someone at the center of everything dies, the first hours are chaos. People don't believe it. Someone insists the doctors are wrong. Someone else can't stop crying. Nobody knows what to do next. That's what Medina looked like that Monday. News spread from Aisha's room into the mosque and out into the streets. And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, the strongest-willed man among the companions, stood up in the mosque and refused to accept it. The Prophet ﷺ hasn't died, he said; he'll come back. The crowd was coming apart. Then Abu Bakr rode in from his house at the edge of town. Today, what he said.
screen: `THE FIRST HOURS ARE CHAOS.` → `'UMAR: HE HAS NOT DIED.` → `ABU BAKR RIDES IN.`

segments.voice: Sahih al-Bukhari tells it step by step. Abu Bakr didn't speak to anyone first. He went straight into Aisha's room, where the Prophet lay covered with a cloth. He uncovered his face, bent down and kissed him, and wept, and said: you were good in life, and you are good in death. Then he walked out into the mosque, where 'Umar was still talking, and told him to sit down. And he spoke to the crowd, one of the most remembered sentences in Muslim history: whoever worshiped Muhammad, Muhammad has died. And whoever worships God, God is alive and does not die. Then he recited a verse from the third surah, which in Pickthall's translation begins: "Muhammad is but a messenger," and goes on to say that messengers had passed away before him, and asks: if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? It was a verse they all knew. It had come down years earlier, after the battle of Uhud. But the companion Ibn 'Abbas said later that it was as if the people had never heard it until Abu Bakr recited it that day. And 'Umar said: when I heard it, my legs gave way, and I fell to the ground, and I knew he had died. Notice what Abu Bakr did. He loved the Prophet as much as anyone alive. He wept over him first. And then he pointed everyone past the man they loved, to the One who does not die. Grief and faith, in the same hour, and neither one canceled the other.
screen: `HE KISSED HIM AND WEPT.` · `WHOEVER WORSHIPED MUHAMMAD...` · `MUHAMMAD IS BUT A MESSENGER.` · `'UMAR'S LEGS GAVE WAY.` · then, large: `ALLAH IS ALIVE AND DOES NOT DIE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice. Sit, and breathe. Think of something or someone you've built your days around, a person, a job, a routine, a place, and imagine for a moment that it's gone. Let yourself feel it; Abu Bakr wept first. Then ask: what's still here underneath? If you pray, you can say quietly: Allah lives. Muslims call God al-Hayy, the Living. If you don't pray, just rest on whatever in you feels steady. The bell holds the time.
Abu Bakr's words. Whoever worshiped Muhammad, Muhammad has died; whoever worships God, God is alive and does not die. Today's word.
Your line: allah is alive and does not die. Today, when something you lean on wobbles, let yourself feel it, and then look for what's steady underneath. Day two hundred ninety-one.

howItsDone: Muslims love and honor the Prophet deeply while worshiping God alone, and Abu Bakr's words on the day he died are often quoted to explain that distinction; God is called al-Hayy, the Living.

fork.setup: you're Abu Bakr. the Prophet ﷺ has died, 'Umar is telling the crowd he hasn't, and the people are coming apart. what do you do first?
options: argue with 'Umar in front of everyone.
go in to the Prophet, kiss him and weep.
call a council to choose a leader.
fork.reveal: he went in first, uncovered the Prophet's face, kissed him and wept. only then did he go out and speak.

original.note: Arabic: the Living, one of the names of God: alive and never dying.

trapdoor: what you thought: a speech at a funeral.
what it means: grief and faith in the same hour: love the Prophet, worship God, who does not die.
what a scholar hears: al-Bukhari's report has Abu Bakr recite 39:30 and 3:144, a verse from after Uhud, which Ibn 'Abbas says the people heard as if for the first time.
